messages:
maria-ops: Heads up — getting multiple customer reports of p99 spikes (~10-12s) on /v1/generate starting ~09:10 UTC. Inflight queue length climbing rapidly for several tenants, tenant-acme is the largest source right now.
ajay-eng: Thanks, pulling metrics now. Link: https://grafana.redwood/rd/alerts/ingress (saw p95 jump 1.2s -> 2.9s, p99 from ~4s -> ~11s).
ingress-bot: Alert: ingress.request_p99 > 8s for service=api, window=5m, severity=high.
sara-support: Customer ticket #12345 (acme) opened; they report timeouts and 503s. They said traffic pattern had a burst of parallel requests from a cron around 09:05.
maria-ops: Quick logs snippet from ingress (09:08-09:12):
```
[09:09:12] admit_queue.len=224 tenant=acme worker=pool-A
[09:09:13] accept=false reason=per-tenant-concurrency tenant=acme current=210 cap=200
[09:09:14] worker.cpu=98% pod=model-worker-12 kv_cache_miss=0.34
[09:09:15] throttle_rejected=37 window=60s
```
kevin-sre: Looks like per-tenant concurrency cap hit + worker saturation on pool-A. Also seeing elevated kv cache evictions which will amplify latency for long conversations. Any recent config changes?
ajay-eng: No config changes in last 24h. I see autoscaler didn't kick because GPUs are at 100% and node group is at max size.
maria-ops: Immediate mitigation proposals: 1) temporarily reduce tenant-acme concurrency cap; 2) enable fallback routing of acme to lower-capacity pool (burstpool) or smaller model; 3) scale up node group if cloud quota allows. Which is fastest?
kevin-sre: Order of speed: reduce per-tenant cap (control-plane flag) and inform them to backoff (fast). Fallback route requires policy change and verification. Scaling nodes might be blocked by cloud quota — I'd try cap first.
sara-support: I'll message the customer to ask them to throttle while we mitigate.
ajay-eng: Quick command to lower cap (control plane API):
```
curl -X POST https://control-plane.internal/tenants/acme/limits \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN' \
  -d '{"concurrency_limit":100}'
```
(we currently have 200).
maria-ops: Applying now. Patch sent.
[09:11:05] ingress-bot: Config change applied: tenant=acme concurrency_limit 200 -> 100 by maria-ops
[09:11:45] maria-ops: Scaling model-worker deployment pool-A +2 replicas as a follow-up (kubectl scale deployment/model-worker-pool-a --replicas=10).
ajay-eng: After cap change and +2 replicas, quick smoke: p95 fell to ~1.6s, p99 to ~3.8s over the 1-minute window. Not fully back to baseline but much improved.
kevin-sre: Good. Next steps: investigate why autoscaler didn't add nodes earlier — check ASG limits and scale-out events. Also check batching config; if batch sizes jumped it can worsen tail latency.
maria-ops: Repro steps for engineering: 1) simulate fan-in with tenant-acme API key at concurrency=250 for 2m; 2) capture admit_controller metrics and model-worker CPU+KV metrics; 3) check worker logs for long garbage collection / OOM.
sara-support: I'll update the ticket: short-term cap + scaling helped; engineering will follow up with root-cause and quota checks. Customer asked for ETA for full fix.
kevin-sre: Owner: ajay-eng to look into autoscaler/gce quota and batching; maria-ops to run heap/profile on model-worker-12; follow-up in 2h.
maria-ops: Also scheduling a rolling restart of pool-A to flush KV cache if we see sustained tail after metrics converge.
ajay-eng: Noted. Adding a perf test to the docket to evaluate batch-size vs tail latency.
kevin-sre: Closing the escalation for now — customer notified and short-term mitigations applied. Will reopen if p99 > 6s again. :thumbsup:
